what it is
rows: The widths of the brain's hidden layers, in order from input to output.
How many numbers one message holds. Each agent sends one message to itself and one to each neighbour, every phase.
Whether every phase begins with an extra look in which agents only write messages, so the look that acts reads messages written this phase.
Whether a parent may move some of its own connections to its newborn child.
Whether a brain changes only when it is copied — into a newborn, or into a node its owner has just won — instead of also after every game, wherever it sits.
How many times over an agent's stake on its own node counts when the game decides who takes the node. 1 is the old rule.
How many of its parent's neighbours a newborn is joined to, drawn at random, besides its parent itself; 0 leaves every link to the brain's choice.
Whether the neighbours of an agent that dies are joined up where its death would leave them in separate pieces.
How many neighbours the two ends of an unused connection must share for it to be cut; 0 cuts every unused connection.
The most connections an agent's brain may choose to hold (0 = no limit). An agent at its limit cannot have a child.
The share of an agent's tokens — rounded up, never less than one — that stays on its own node whatever its brain says; a parent also keeps one. 0 is the old rule.
The age at which an agent dies (0 = never); its tokens are shared out like those of any other dead agent.
The fewest tokens a child can be born with; a parent that would give less has no child.
